chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Munakhkhal, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
Jibra'il عليه السلام descended with this verse upon Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله like this:
Evil is that for which they sold their souls: that they should disbelieve in what Allah revealed concerning Ali, out of envy.

key_terms.أَنْ يَكْفُرُوا: that they should disbelieve or reject
key_terms.اشْتَرَوْا: they sold or exchanged, meaning they traded away something precious
key_terms.الْآيَةِ: the verse being cited and explained
key_terms.بَغْيًا: out of envy, insolence, or rebellious hostility
key_terms.بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ: in what Allah sent down as revelation
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلُ: Jibra'il عليه السلام, the angel who brought revelation

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain Qur'an 2:90 in relation to Ali عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This narration presents a recited form of the verse as explained by Imam Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, linking its meaning to what Allah revealed concerning Ali عليه السلام. It is used in the context of wilayah and shows a tafsir-oriented reading emphasizing rejection of divinely revealed authority out of hostility and envy.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Barqy, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ammar Bin Marwan, from Munakhhal, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
Jibraeelas descended with this Verse like this
[2:90] Evil is that for which they have sold their souls - that they should deny what Allah has Revealed regarding Aliasws, in rebellion’.
en.sarwar: 25. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi from his father Muhammad ibn Sinan from ‘Ammar ibn Marwan from Munakhkhal from Jabir from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following.
“Evil is that for which they have sold their souls: They have refused to accept God’s revelations (about Leadership with Divine Authority of Ali (a.s.)) in rebellion. .” [2:90]”
